newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European markets end sharply up, led by NYK.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European markets end sharply up, led by NYK.

text.p: Several European stock markets hit all-time highs on Wednesday as Wall Street extended its record run initially, but the markets all pared gains after Federal Reserve vice-chairman Alice Rivlin warned that the risk for the U.S. economy remained on the upside.
"The risks seem higher on the other side (of recession), that many of the factors holding down inflationary pressures will prove temporary," Rivlin said.

Germany, France, Italy, Belgium, the Netherlands and Austria notched record highs as the Dow Jones Industrial Average added about 80 points to Tuesday's 155-point gain before edging off on some profit-taking after Rivlin's comments.

The Dow closed at a record high on Tuesday after Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan predicted moderate U.S. growth and low inflation this year. Greenspan will finish his Humphrey-Hawkins testimony later on Wednesday.
But the Dow retreated later on Wednesday and was up only 37.39 points at 8,099.04 in late European trading.
The dollar also gave back some gains after Rivlin said in her testimony to the House Banking Committee that the currency may not get much stronger.

Earlier, the dollar jumped to a six-year high against the mark and a one-year high against the French franc, which added lustre to German and French export prospects as the weaker currencies make their goods cheaper abroad.
The dollar was also supported by general mark weakness from continuing doubts over the health of European economic and monetary union.

Germany's DAX index surged 4.15 percent to post its biggest daily gain this year and ended bourse trading up 175.67 points at 4,406.09. But that was off its intraday high of 4,418.64, scored before bourse trade was temporarily suspended just after midday due to a systems problem.
Some analysts predicted the DAX above 5,000 within two weeks.
Paris added about three percent to close at a record peak.
Germany's DAX index and France's CAC-40 index also got a lift from rising bank shares. Bank stocks jumped on merger speculation and solid earnings reports.

Monday's news that Bayerische Vereinsbank AG and Bayerische Hypobank would merge had already fired up investors, who believe that a long-awaited consolidation of the fragmented banking sector might be under way.
Germany's largest bank, Deutsche Bank AG helped sentiment by reporting a 27.5-percent rise in net income. The result, above forecasts, sent its shares surging to an all-time high of 132 earlier.
Banque Nationale de Paris and Crdit Commercial de France in France also climbed. Credit Commercial gained more than 10 percent to notch a year high of 300.0.
Italian stocks got an added boost from tame July inflation data. Preliminary July consumer price data showed inflation flat from June and at a 1.6-percent pace, year-over-year.
Italy's blue-chip Mib30 index hit a record 23,375 and the all-share Mibtel notched a record 15,311.

Belgium jumped nearly 2.5 percent to a record high 2,606.88, Austria's ATX index climbed 3.15 percent to an all-time high of 1,452.78 and Dutch shares ended almost three-percent higher at a record peak.
Dutch traders expected stocks to correct lower soon but retain their overall bullish sentiment.

French, German, Italian and British government debt prices also rallied to new highs, lowering interest rates and lending even more support to stocks. U.S. 30-year bond yields slid at New York's open to 6.41 percent, their lowest level since December 5.
"Greenspan is painting a picture of moderate growth and inflation under control, and all bond markets like that," a dealer on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange said.

"Interest rates are falling, stock markets are rising...and everything is fine," said a broker in Helsinki, where the FOX index ended up about 1.25 percent but failed to break its record high of 1,226.84 set on July 17.
London's FTSE-100 index rose but remained the laggard among major European bourses.
"We had a very good rally on the back of Wall Street, but what is more interesting is that it didn't last," said a dealer in London.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.8235 marks and 115.73 yen versus 1.8177 and 115.54 in late trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended up 27.8 points at 4,874.50.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index ended bourse trade up 175.67 points at 4,406.09.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 82.40 points at 3,003.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed in London at 1500 GMT at $324.90, down from $327.95 at Tuesday's close. Silver was firm at $4.33 .
